messages:
carmen: spotting weirdness in Rollouts -> Global p99 for /v1/chat this morning: global rollup shows 1.3s, but region breakdowns are 420-480ms per region. p50/p95 line up. anyone seen multi-region fanout cause this?

lee: hmm multi-region fanout + model-fallback could do it. if a request fans out to region A + B and we aggregate sketches naively you can double-count retries or fallback latencies.

natalie: also possible: rollup cache TTLs. aggregator keeps a cached merged sketch for global view and we rotated routing rules earlier — cache may have stale sketches from before the change.

carmen: query we use for global rollup:
```
SELECT quantile(0.99)(latency_ms) FROM global_trace_rollups WHERE route_alias='chat-prod' AND window='5m' /* merged from per-region sketches */
```
and region pane uses
```
SELECT quantiles(0.5,0.95,0.99)(latency_ms) FROM region_traces WHERE endpoint='/v1/chat' GROUP BY region
```

ops-bot: deploy "route-multi-region-fallback" applied 2026-04-01T07:12:10Z. global_rollup_cache.ttl=300s -> 900s during rollout.

lee: that explains TTL part. increasing TTL during rollout was to reduce churn, but if sketches change shape after route change we could end up showing an overheated global p99 for a while. the cache length plus merge semantics matter.

natalie: I checked logs: a spike of long-tail requests went to the fallback model in one AZ for ~2m, and aggregator cached merged sketch that included fallback latencies. region panes later reported lower numbers because they compute from fresh worker histograms.

carmen: oh wow. so global view combined old cached high-tail sketch with fresh small-tail sketches from other regions -> inflated p99. ugly.

lee: two separate issues then: (1) cached merged sketches with long TTL can show stale extremes, (2) fanout/fallback can introduce duplicates if we don't dedupe by request_id when building global sketches.

natalie: quick mitigation: 1) purge global_rollup_cache for affected window, 2) set cache.ttl back to 60s while we patch dedupe logic. I'll trigger purge.

ops-bot: cache-purge "global-rollup" for window 2026-04-01T07:05:00Z -> 2026-04-01T07:15:00Z executed at 2026-04-01T07:27:00Z.

carmen: cool. can someone run a recompute from raw events for that 10m window to sanity-check p99?

lee: running recompute now (small script):
```python
# recompute weighted p99 across regions
events = fetch_events(route='chat-prod', window='2026-04-01T07:05:00Z/2026-04-01T07:15:00Z')
# dedupe by request_id preferring worker-final latency
unique = dedupe_by_request_id(events)
print(percentile(unique.latency_ms, 99))
```

natalie: recompute result posted: recompute-p99=468ms; region-max-p99=482ms; global-rollup-before-purge=1.3s; global-rollup-after-purge=476ms. parity restored.

lee: good. follow-ups: a) add request_id dedupe when merging sketches for global rollups, b) surface cache_ttl and last-merge-time in the UI as a small provenance pill, c) prevent extending TTL during route experiments without approval.

carmen: UI ask: provenance pill should include: quantile_source (merged-region-tdigest | recompute-weighted | host-hist), last_merge_time, cache_ttl, total_sample_count, dedupe_status. shows why numbers differ without digging.

natalie: agreed. also we need an API debate: expose include_retries & dedupe_by_request_id flags on the public /metrics/rollups endpoint or keep them internal? ops wants them internal to prevent downstream consumers breaking.

lee: my take: expose them but default to safe values and mark as "advanced". users can opt-in if they understand semantics. otherwise people will misinterpret numbers.

ocps-bot: (typo)

ops-bot: filed MET-4822 "Global rollup dedupe + provenance pill + cache guardrails" assigned to natalie.

carmen: thanks. natalie, after MET-4822 lands can we add an automated check that alerts when global_rollup.last_merge_time > max(region.last_report_time) + 120s for a route? that'll catch stale caches.

natalie: yes. adding to ticket. also add a note in rollout checklist: avoid increasing rollup cache TTL during heavy routing experiments.

lee: long-term: prefer recompute-weighted for p99 for global SLOs when sample_count < 10k or when dedupe_rate > 1.2x; merged sketches are useful for high-throughput medians but dangerous at extremes. doc in runbook.

carmen: perfect. closing loop: purge fixed the panic, MET-4822 to track fixes, we'll push provenance pill + TTL UI next week. :rocket:
